persons.name: Austin Scott Miller
persons.role: Last commander of the Resolute Support Mission and top U.S. general in Afghanistan during the withdrawal
persons.status_detail: Testified in a closed-door House Foreign Affairs Committee session. Relinquished command in mid-July 2021.

family.name: unnamed son (serving in the military, received calls during the withdrawal)

mentions.quote: Today we're going to talk about General Miller, the last commander of Resolute Support Mission in Afghanistan.
Bill and Tom Joscelyn, really, you know, we were pulling this apart by district... but I didn't disagree. And then later he says, they had it right.
he did relinquish command in mid July.

persons.name: Zalmay Khalilzad
persons.role: U.S. Special Representative for Afghanistan Reconciliation; architect of the Doha deal with the Taliban
persons.status_detail: Previously testified before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where he said AQIS was defeated and extinguished in Afghanistan.

mentions.quote: We had Zalme-Calizade... the special representative for Afghanistan reconciliation
it's inconsistent with Zalme-Kul-Azad said... he was saying that AQIS... was defeated and extinguished from Afghanistan

persons.name: Mike Pompeo
persons.role: U.S. Secretary of State during the Trump administration

mentions.quote: he had access to Secretary Pompeo.

persons.name: Kenneth McKenzie
persons.role: CENTCOM commander; in Miller's chain of command during the Biden administration

mentions.quote: he had to report to General McKenzie, the SINCOM commander

persons.name: Joe Biden
persons.role: U.S. president who oversaw the August 2021 withdrawal from Afghanistan

mentions.quote: when the Biden administration comes in, General Miller is locked out of the interagency process

persons.name: Ashraf Ghani
persons.role: Afghan president at the time of the withdrawal

mentions.quote: if Ashrafgani isn't the guy and your current chain of the command isn't working

persons.name: Ayman al-Zawahiri
persons.status_detail: Killed in a U.S. drone strike in Kabul in 2022.

mentions.quote: Zawahiri being drone to death in his victory villa inside Kabul in 2022

persons.name: John Nicholson
persons.role: Former U.S. commander in Afghanistan; Bill mentions him while recalling the 2019 decision to stop district reporting
persons.status_detail: The hosts are unsure which general gave the 'limited decision-making value' quote. Bill says Miller discontinued the reporting but also names Nicholson.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Its goal is to resurrect the Islamic Emirate. The hosts say it used diplomacy as part of a military solution and took over through both negotiation and military operations.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: The hosts say al-Qaeda is intertwined with the Taliban and 'marbled throughout'; Miller agreed that senior leadership remained in Afghanistan.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent
organizations.notes: Miller said it had camps in Afghanistan. This contradicts Khalilzad's claim that it was defeated.

organizations.name: Islamic State
organizations.notes: Miller viewed ISIS as the greater international threat. The hosts argue it was never going to take over Afghanistan.

organizations.name: House Foreign Affairs Committee
organizations.notes: Held the closed-door Miller testimony of more than 200 pages.

organizations.name: US State Department
organizations.notes: Criticized for assuming it could keep an embassy in Kabul without military protection and for planning the NEO too late.

organizations.name: US Central Command
organizations.notes: Miller reported through its commander, McKenzie.

organizations.name: Afghan government
organizations.notes: The hosts say its officials did not believe the U.S. was leaving.

organizations.name: Afghan War Commission
organizations.notes: The hosts doubt it will deliver real accountability because its members were involved in the war.

events.description: Miller testified in a closed-door session of about nine to ten hours before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, producing more than 200 pages of transcript.
Joscelyn's article for The Dispatch argued that the situation in Afghanistan was much worse than the U.S. military claimed.
The U.S. military stopped releasing district-control data, calling it of limited decision-making value and saying the goal was a political settlement.
Zawahiri was killed in a U.S. drone strike in Kabul.
The U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan and the Taliban takeover.

relationships.detail: During the Biden administration Miller reported through the CENTCOM commander and had little direct input.
relationships.quote: he had to report to General McKenzie, the SINCOM commander

relationships.detail: Miller had access to Pompeo during the Trump administration.
relationships.quote: he had access to Secretary Pompeo

relationships.detail: Miller worked alongside Khalilzad on the effort to find a Taliban power broker and negotiate a political settlement.
relationships.quote: he talks about going with Kalilazade... to try and find somebody to negotiate with the Taliban

relationships.detail: Khalilzad negotiated the Doha deal in which the hosts say the Taliban fleeced the U.S.
The hosts describe a Taliban-al-Qaeda axis, with al-Qaeda marbled throughout the Taliban.
Zawahiri was killed by a drone in a villa in Kabul in 2022.
relationships.quote: Zawahiri being drone to death in his victory villa inside Kabul in 2022

relationships.detail: Miller confirmed AQIS had camps and operated throughout Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: talks about AQAS having camps and still operating throughout Afghanistan

Special counsel report on President Biden's classified documents
key_claims: Miller recognized that the Taliban's goal was to resurrect the Islamic Emirate, which is incompatible with a political settlement.
The Taliban was eager to negotiate with the U.S. and the hosts say it got what it wanted.
The hosts say the Taliban used diplomacy to weaken the Afghan government as part of its military solution.
Miller said al-Qaeda was present in Afghanistan throughout the war, contradicting Khalilzad's claim that AQIS was defeated.
The hosts argue the State Department wrongly assumed it could keep an embassy in Kabul and that the NEO was called too late.
Afghan officials did not believe the U.S. was leaving, and the U.S. kept them fighting for a draw while the Taliban fought to win.
Miller was locked out of Biden-era interagency decision-making, which limited his influence.
The hosts say the U.S. military stopped publishing district-control data in 2019 because it was inconvenient.
